record.vts_authority: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung des Bundes (GDWS / WSA Weser-Jade-Nordsee)
record.vts_sector: German Bight Traffic (VHF 16/79/80; statutory Inner German Bight = VHF 80 coverage area)
record.vts_boundary_basis: AnlBV Anhang chart (Q-S2), the statutory definition of the Inner German Bight, is the area covered by German Bight Traffic VHF channel 80. On it, the area boundary crosses TSS Terschelling-German Bight at about 006°16'-006°22'E (estimated from the chart graticule), so the German section east of there is inside. AnlBV Nr. 5.1 states traffic there is monitored under maritime traffic safety and Nr. 3.1 requires reports to 'Verkehrszentrale German Bight Traffic' (Q-S1). ELWIS lists German Bight Traffic as a VTS sector of Verkehrszentrale Wilhelmshaven covering the sea area between Ems and Elbe (Q-S3). WSA states Wilhelmshaven monitors the inner German Bight from Borkum to Helgoland (Q-S6). The Dutch western section (to about 006°16'E) is not shown to be in any VTS.
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). German part: AnlBV Nr. 3.1 entry report (ships over 300 GT, at 007°10'E or 54°20'N) and SeeSchStrO § 58 reports are made to German Bight Traffic, a VTS, so they are recorded as VTS reporting, not a separate MRS (Q-S1, Q-S20). Dutch part: STZ art. 5(1) territorial-sea entry reporting may apply where the lanes enter the Dutch territorial sea, but its operation is unconfirmed (Q-S10).
record.evidence_summary: Statutory chart and AnlBV place the German section of TSS Terschelling-German Bight inside the German Bight Traffic (VHF 80) Inner German Bight area. German Bight Traffic is a VTS sector of Verkehrszentrale Wilhelmshaven established under SOLAS V/12. Coverage is partial; the Dutch section is not covered by any VTS shown. Coastguard wave-height advice is voluntary route advice (Q-S19).
record.source_date: Q-S2 BGBl. I 2005 p. 2297 (current Anhang); Q-S1 current consolidation accessed 29 Sep 2026; Q-S5 18 Aug 2017
record.unresolved_issue: Precise boundary longitude (chart-scale estimate about 006°16'-006°22'E, 2005 chart; TSS geometry since amended). Whether German Bight Traffic's western area (VHF 79, lead Q-S21) extends further west than the VHF 80 Inner German Bight. Status of Dutch STZ art. 5(1) reporting and Brandaris approach-area buoy 'TG' position.
record.vts_leads: Brandaris approach area (Dutch, zeegat van Terschelling; buoy 'TG' named in its limits), coverage not shown. German Bight Traffic western area VHF 79 (lead only, Q-S21).
record.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed with corrected basis: VTS only (partial). The lead's GDWS Bekanntmachung 19.1.4/19.1.5 (Borkumriff and TG 17/C reports) could not be retrieved; coverage now rests on the statutory AnlBV Anhang chart.

record.vts_authority: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung des Bundes (GDWS / WSA Weser-Jade-Nordsee)
record.vts_sector: German Bight Traffic (VHF 80 area / Inner German Bight)
record.vts_boundary_basis: AnlBV Nr. 3.1 names the TSS and requires ships entering the Inner German Bight from the west to report to German Bight Traffic at 007°10'E, whether or not they use GBWA (Q-S1). On the AnlBV Anhang chart (Q-S2) the Inner German Bight (VHF 80 area) boundary runs north-south at about 007°18'E and crosses only the easternmost few miles of the TSS; the TSS's main length to the west lies outside. So coverage by German Bight Traffic is partial (eastern end). The western part lies in the outer German Bight, where ELWIS lists Verkehrszentrale Cuxhaven 'Äußere Deutsche Bucht' with sector German North Sea Traffic (Q-S3), but no boundary shows it includes the TSS.
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). AnlBV Nr. 3.1 report at 007°10'E (over 300 GT) is made to German Bight Traffic (VTS reporting, national statute). AnlBV Nr. 6 (mandatory use of GBWA by large tankers) and the IMO mandatory tanker route (Q-S14) are routeing, not reporting, measures.
record.evidence_summary: GBWA is named in AnlBV Nr. 3.1 and Nr. 6. Only its eastern end lies inside the statutory German Bight Traffic (VHF 80) area; most of its length is in the outer German Bight EEZ. VTS only on a partial-coverage basis. German North Sea Traffic (Cuxhaven) is a lead for the western part.
record.source_date: Q-S2 BGBl. I 2005 p. 2297; Q-S1 current consolidation accessed 29 Sep 2026
record.unresolved_issue: Whether German North Sea Traffic (VTS Centre Cuxhaven, 'Äußere Deutsche Bucht') has a defined area including the GBWA lanes (BSH VTS Guide Germany 2026 section C5.1 not freely available). Current IMO geometry of GBWA against the 2005 chart boundary (about 007°18'E) and the 007°10'E reporting meridian.
record.vts_leads: German North Sea Traffic (Verkehrszentrale Cuxhaven), outer German Bight, boundary not verified.
record.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: VTS only retained but coverage restricted to the eastern end; the lead did not note that most of the TSS lies west of the Inner German Bight boundary.

record.vts_authority: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung des Bundes (GDWS / WSA Weser-Jade-Nordsee)
record.vts_sector: German Bight Traffic (VHF 80 area / Inner German Bight)
record.vts_boundary_basis: AnlBV Nr. 8 places the pilot transfer position 'im Verkehrstrennungsgebiet "Jade Approach"' within the Inner German Bight outside the territorial sea (Q-S1). The Inner German Bight is statutorily the German Bight Traffic VHF 80 coverage area (Q-S2); on that chart the Jade Approach lies well inside the area (east of the about 007°18'E boundary, south-west of Helgoland) and adjacent to the territorial sea boundary. Nr. 5.1: traffic monitored under maritime traffic safety. Consistent with WSA 'inner German Bight from Borkum to Helgoland' (Q-S6).
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). AnlBV Nr. 3.1 and SeeSchStrO § 58 reports go to German Bight Traffic/Jade Traffic (VTS reporting).
record.evidence_summary: Statute names the Jade Approach TSS as lying in the Inner German Bight, which the statutory chart defines as the German Bight Traffic VHF 80 area; the whole TSS lies inside that area on the chart. VTS only.
record.source_date: Q-S2 BGBl. I 2005 p. 2297; Q-S1 current consolidation accessed 29 Sep 2026
record.unresolved_issue: Coverage 'full' relies on the 2005 statutory chart; Jade Approach geometry may have been amended since (IMO instrument not retrieved), but any amendment near 54°N 007°30'-007°45'E would remain well inside the area.
record.vts_leads: Jade Traffic (Verkehrszentrale Wilhelmshaven) for the Jade fairway inshore of the TSS.
record.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: VTS only, basis strengthened with the AnlBV Anhang chart.

record.vts_authority: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung des Bundes (GDWS / WSA Weser-Jade-Nordsee)
record.vts_sector: German Bight Traffic (VHF 80 area / Inner German Bight); Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic adjoins from Tonne Elbe
record.vts_boundary_basis: On the AnlBV Anhang chart (Q-S2), the Elbe approach TSS (near 54°00'N 008°05'E on the 2005 chart) lies deep inside the German Bight Traffic VHF 80 coverage arc and east of the about 007°18'E boundary. The GDWS SeeSchStrO Bekanntmachung (Q-S7) makes Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic responsible from Tonne Elbe inward, with outbound vessels reporting at Tonne Elbe to German Bight Traffic on VHF 80, so the TSS seaward of Tonne Elbe falls to German Bight Traffic. ELWIS/WSA describe Cuxhaven as covering the 'Elbeansteuerung' (Q-S3, Q-S8). Both are sectors of the German coastal VTS; the TSS is covered either way.
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). SeeSchStrO § 58 reports at Tonne Elbe (Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic inbound VHF 71; German Bight Traffic outbound VHF 80) and AnlBV Nr. 3.1 are VTS reporting (Q-S7, Q-S1, Q-S20).
record.evidence_summary: The Elbe approach TSS lies inside the statutory German Bight Traffic VHF 80 area, seaward of the Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic sector boundary at Tonne Elbe. VTS only; the exact split between German Bight Traffic and Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic at the TSS's east end depends on the Tonne Elbe position versus current TSS geometry.
record.source_date: Q-S2 BGBl. I 2005 p. 2297; Q-S7 BAnz AT 31.01.2014 B7 (amended to 2024, Nr. 29.1 not seen amended)
record.unresolved_issue: Current IMO Elbe approach geometry versus Tonne Elbe (sector hand-over), and whether later amendments moved the Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic limit (the prior lead cited Nordergründe-Nord). This affects the sector split, not the VTS association.
record.vts_leads: Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic (Verkehrszentrale Cuxhaven) at the eastern end.
record.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: VTS only confirmed, with German Bight Traffic as primary sector and Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic adjoining from Tonne Elbe; the lead's Nordergründe-Nord sector limit was not verified (2014 text says Tonne Elbe).

record.tss_name: In the approaches to the River Humber
record.vts_authority: Associated British Ports, Humber Estuary Services (Statutory Harbour Authority)
record.vts_sector: Humber Approaches (VHF 14, seaward to No. 4A Clee Ness Light Float meridian)
record.vts_boundary_basis: VTS Humber seaward limit (Q-S16): Easington Church (53°39.02'N 000°06.90'E) 086° to 53°40'N 000°30'E, 180° to 53°30'N 000°30'E, 262° to Donna Nook (53°28.40'N 000°09.23'E). All TSS vertices (Q-S13) lie west of 000°30'E (maximum 000°22.95'E) and south of the northern line (point 36 at 53°38.70'N versus the line at about 53°39.6'N). The southernmost vertex (30) 53°29.19'N 000°19.97'E lies on the 262° line within about 0.04' (charting precision). VTS reporting points are the TSS limb buoys (Outer Binks, Outer Sea Reach, Outer Rosse Reach). TOS is provided from the seaward limit.
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system: WETREP (VRS-0005) meets the UK east coast at 52°12'N and resumes at 58°30'N, so the Humber is outside (Q-S15); no other Part I system in the area. Humber reporting (2.5 h notice, reporting points) is VTS reporting, compulsory for sea-going vessels (Q-S16).
record.evidence_summary: The IMO Humber TSS (COLREG.2/Circ.60, implemented 2009) lies wholly within the published VTS Humber area. VTS Humber is compulsory for sea-going vessels and provides TOS from the seaward limit, with reporting points on the TSS limbs. No MRS.
record.source_date: Q-S16 undated, accessed 29 Sep 2026; Q-S13 10 Dec 2008 / Corr.1 2 Apr 2009
record.unresolved_issue: VTS Humber web page is undated; confirm against ALRS Vol 6 or current Humber standing notices. IMO 2025 may include later amendments to the TSS after 2009 (none found).
